knowledge:
- key_parameters: summ_exp=A SummarizedExperiment object containing the expression/read count matrix ;; mod[, -1]=Model matrix of known factors (covariates) to adjust for, excluding the intercept ;; num.sv=The number of surrogate variables to estimate ;; permute=Logical indicating whether to use permutation to determine the number of significant SVs ;; iasva.sv=Matrix of detected surrogate variables used to find marker genes or study R-squared thresholds
- alternatives: tSNE on all genes=Mentioned as failing to detect rare outlier cells compared to running tSNE on marker genes identified by IA-SVA ;; fast_iasva=A faster implementation of IA-SVA recommended for particularly large datasets
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing bulk or single-cell RNA-Seq data with suspected hidden heterogeneity (e.g., cell subtypes, batch effects, or unmeasured technical/biological variation) that may be correlated with known factors like library size or patient ID.
- pitfalls: Failing to account for geometric library size (or proportion of expressed genes), which explains a large portion of scRNA-Seq variability and correlates highly with PC1 ;; The choice of R-squared threshold in find_markers greatly influences the number of marker genes identified and the quality of downstream clustering; users should use study_R2 to tune this parameter.

workflows.name: hidden_heterogeneity_detection
workflows.intent: Detect hidden sources of variation in single-cell or bulk RNA-Seq data, identify marker genes associated with these sources, and optimize parameters.
input: counts (matrix of read counts where genes are rows, samples are columns)
anns (matrix or data frame of sample annotations/metadata)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate geometric library size as a known covariate ;; 2. Construct the model matrix of known factors ;; 3. Create a SummarizedExperiment object from the counts ;; 4. Run IA-SVA (using iasva or fast_iasva) to detect surrogate variables ;; 5. Find marker genes associated with the detected surrogate variables using find_markers ;; 6. Tune the R-squared threshold using study_R2
workflows.code:
geo_lib_size <- colSums(log(counts + 1))
lcounts <- log(counts + 1)
pc1 <- irlba(lcounts - rowMeans(lcounts), 1)$v[, 1]
cor(geo_lib_size, pc1)
patient_id <- anns$Patient_ID
mod <- model.matrix(~patient_id + geo_lib_size)
summ_exp <- SummarizedExperiment(assays = counts)
iasva.res<- iasva(summ_exp, mod[, -1],verbose = FALSE, 
                  permute = FALSE, num.sv = 5)
iasva.sv <- iasva.res$sv
cor(geo_lib_size, iasva.sv[, 1])
marker.counts <- find_markers(summ_exp, as.matrix(iasva.sv[,1]))
iasva.res <- fast_iasva(summ_exp, mod[, -1], num.sv = 5)
study_res <- study_R2(summ_exp, iasva.sv)
